_comment: V3 of the Salman Farsi / Just Ask Expo reel -- v2 with the P1 hook take removed and NOTHING else changed by choice. Every absolute time on the output timeline is v2's minus 5.80s (P1's length); everything anchor-resolved (hero_words, badges, documents) is byte-identical because it is keyed to spoken words, not clock time. Total content is 20.27s (was 26.07s). v1 and v2 are finished and delivered; this is a separate folder and leaves both untouched.
_asr_note: Same corrections as v1/v2: only 'counselor' -> Australian 'counsellor' for on-screen text. P2 transcribed cleanly as 'One event, one afternoon, every answer.' with a trailing self-cue 'Okay' that is trimmed via clips.json, not asr_fix.
_name_note: Times unchanged from v2 (0.6-4.0), which now places the lower-third over the head of P2 instead of P1. Checked against the asset rather than assumed: the card sits bottom-left (x 45-375, y ~1490-1580), P2's close-up burns ONE EVENT mid-left at y ~900-1200, and its walking shot burns ONE AFTERNOON along the pavement bottom-RIGHT from x ~640. The card clears both.
_mara_note: Salman is an Education Counsellor, not a Registered Migration Agent -- no MARN exists for him, so mara.mode is 'none'. Never invent one. The script separately mentions migration agents will be AT the expo, which is a statement about the event, not about him.
_hook_banner_note: REMOVED on request. It read 'STUCK ON YOUR COURSE? 🤔' at 0.0-1.5 and was carried over verbatim from v2, where it sat over the P1 hook take and echoed his spoken line. Once P1 went, it was a question the reel no longer asks: nothing in the remaining audio sets up 'stuck', so it read as a leftover caption over an opening that already carries its own burned-in ONE EVENT super. Disabled the way build_captions.py's own default expresses it -- empty text, zero-length window -- rather than deleting the key, because the JS guard is `HB && HB.text && HB.end > HB.start`, so an empty string renders nothing at all and the block stays here as a record of what was dropped. NOTE the word STUCK is deliberately still in `gold`: that list only tints spoken caption words, and 'stuck' is no longer anywhere in this cut's audio, so the entry is inert -- left in place so the list stays identical to v1/v2 rather than diverging for no visible effect.
_cap_top_note: Left at the 62% default. P3 frames him small with his face high (~39% of frame height). P2 is a multicam clip whose close-up puts his face far higher still, and whose wide walking shot puts it lower -- but captions are suppressed across that whole segment anyway (see _hero_note4), so it never competes.
_hero_note: FOUR silent entries, none of which render anything themselves -- each exists only to suppress the plain 2-word caption cards over a window that already carries its own text or graphic. build_captions.py suppresses a card when the card's START falls inside the window, which is why some anchors deliberately begin one word early. All four are ANCHOR-resolved, so removing P1 shifts their windows automatically and this block needed no edits.
_hero_note4: The FOURTH entry covers the supplied P2, which has ONE EVENT / ONE AFTERNOON / EVERY ANSWER burned into the picture -- the reel's own captions would otherwise print those same three phrases a second time, in smaller type, over the top of them. The window now resolves to 0.10-4.33 (v2: 5.90-10.13), i.e. the entire P2 segment, which is now also the entire opening of the reel; the next card ('Is' at 4.609) falls outside it and inside the searchmg window instead, so nothing is left uncovered.

hero_words.anchor_phrase: One event, one afternoon, every answer
on 25th of August from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m.
There will be university representative, migration agent, and education counsellor

_badges_note: ONE badge, unchanged from v2 and anchor-resolved. The EVERY ANSWER badge was dropped back in v2 because the new P2 burns EVERY ANSWER into the picture itself. FREE ENTRY stays on 'by PFEC Global' (measured resolve: 6.24s), which is clear of the searchmg cutaway ending at 5.97.
_documents_note: The Just Ask Expo campaign banner, anchored to the CITIES line so it lands on the words its artwork illustrates. Width 620 at top:1150px so it reads as a secondary flyer card BELOW cities_behind.py's photo band (which runs y=0..960, feathered from 880) rather than competing with it. Anchor-resolved, so unchanged by P1's removal.

documents.anchor_phrase: in our Melbourne, Sydney, and Adelaide office

_decor_note: Orbs and sparkles only -- no @PFECGlobal handle pill, same as v1/v2.
_zoom_note: hits[] are keyed by clip index with 'at' in RAW clip time. CHANGED FROM V2 ONLY BY RE-INDEXING: dropping P1 shifts every clip index down one, so the index map is now 0:P2 1:P3a 2:P3b 3:P3c and the punch on P3c moves from clip 4 to clip 3. Its 'at' window is RAW clip time and therefore untouched. The segments[] list likewise just loses P1's leading 'in': hold / out / in / hold across the four cuts, so no two adjacent segments move the same way and the brief's zoom ins and outs are still intact. Segment 0 stays 'hold' because the AI multicam P2 already snaps between a close-up and a wide walking shot on its own -- a pipeline push-zoom would fight camera motion the asset is built around.
_music_note: 'Cloud Dancer' (Kevin MacLeod, CC BY 4.0), same as v1/v2. Licence block is already in assets/music/CREDIT.txt.
_ducking_note: duck_ratio 8 / duck_threshold 0.05 with the bed at 0.44, carried over from v2 unchanged. v2 arrived at 0.44 by measurement, not taste: the reel's peak source is his VOICE, not the SFX transients, and the voice bus has no compression of its own, so a near-constant bed simply stacked on top of it. Real ducking pulls the bed under every phrase so the two stop summing. Two traps worth remembering: LOWERING SFX volumes made the true peak WORSE (quieter cues drop integrated loudness, so the two-pass loudnorm applies more static gain and lifts the voice peaks with it), and softening the duck to 6/0.07 blew the peak straight back out. v2 lifted the bed 0.38 -> 0.44 because the replacement P2 carries a 1.56s unducked pause between 'afternoon' and 'every answer' that raised the programme's dynamic range; that pause is still here, and P1's removal takes away 5.80s of fairly continuous speech, which if anything raises LRA further. RE-MEASURE WITH qa_reel RATHER THAN ADJUSTING BY EAR, and treat that pause -- now at 1.23-2.79, i.e. in the reel's first three seconds -- as the first spot to listen to.
_truepeak_note: KNOWN, ACCEPTED WARN: this cut measures -0.5 dBTP against the pipeline's -1 dBTP target (v2 shipped at -1.3). qa_reel reports it as WARN, not FAIL, and the flat-factor check finds NO clipped samples -- it is a headroom-margin shortfall, not audible distortion. Root cause, measured rather than guessed: build_composite appends a fixed ~6.2s of quiet end cards, which is 23% of this 26.5s reel against 19% of v2's 32.3s, so the same speech now averages out to a quieter programme. work/mixed.mp4 lands at -20.8 LUFS with a -3.2 dBTP peak (a 17.6 dB peak-to-loudness ratio), loudnorm therefore needs +6.8 dB, that would put the peak at +3.6, so it REFUSES the requested linear=true and falls back to normalization_type=dynamic; alimiter then clamps and the AAC encode overshoots on decode. DO NOT try to tune this by sweeping the music bed or the SFX volumes. That surface was measured across ten full rebuilds and it is chaotic, not monotonic: bed 0.32 -> -0.8, 0.38 -> +3.2 (FAIL), 0.44 -> -0.5, 0.50 -> +0.3 (FAIL); SFX x0.50 -> -1.0 (OK), x0.55 -> -0.3, x0.60 -> +3.1 (FAIL). Every one of those reproduces exactly on a rebuild, and neighbouring settings measure input_i identically (-20.81) and input_tp within 0.03 dB, so a passing value is where dynamic mode's gain trajectory happens to land, NOT a principled optimum -- it would not survive any future edit to this reel. Scaling every SFX cue by 0.50 does measure -1.0 dBTP at an unchanged -14.3 LUFS if a clean gate is ever required, but it halves cues that were already at v1's low measured-safe levels (whoosh 0.20 -> 0.10, tick 0.17 -> 0.085), so it buys the number by making the Tier-1 pass nearly inaudible under a 0.44 bed. Also confirmed here: halving the SFX moved the mix's own peak by only 0.03 dB, which independently re-proves v2's finding that the peak source is his VOICE, not the cues. The real fix, if this ever becomes a FAIL rather than a WARN, is compression on the voice bus -- which build_composite does not currently expose -- or a shorter/louder end-card tail.
_sfx_note: NINE cues, down from v2's ten. Every surviving cue is v2's value -5.80s. The deletion is v2's transition-whoosh at 5.80: that masked the P1->P2 cut, which no longer exists. Remaining transition-whooshes sit on each of the 3 real cuts (4.37 / 10.82 / 13.92, taken from broll_plan.json's boundaries); pop.mp3 on the two date-plate slams (the P3a segment starts 4.37, plate entrances are local 3.30 and 4.90 -> 7.67 and 9.27); tick.mp3 on each city name; success-chime under the CTA. pop and tick attack at sample 0 so they sit ON the beat with no offset. Volumes are v1/v2's measured-safe set -- see _ducking_note before touching them.
_thumbnail_note: MOVED, and this is the one field P1's removal forced a real decision on rather than arithmetic. v2 grabbed 3.2s, a clean mid-hook frame inside P1. Straight subtraction is not an option (it goes negative) and leaving 3.2 alone lands inside P2, where the frame carries the burned-in EVERY ANSWER super and he is small and far from camera -- the still's own headline is 'ONE EVENT. EVERY ANSWER', so it would have printed those words twice. 6.80 is the equivalent clean frame in the P3a segment: after the searchmg cutaway ends (5.97), before the date plate enters (7.67), and clear of the wipe at 4.37. Verified on the frame itself -- full-body, eyes open, no burned-in type.

caption_txt.title: The One Event You Can't Skip — Just Ask Expo, 25 August
body: Still stuck on which course actually suits you? Still not sure which institution fits your goals? Stop guessing — just ask.

The PFEC Global Just Ask Expo is on 25 August, 2 to 5 PM, at our Melbourne, Sydney and Adelaide offices. University representatives, migration agents and education counsellors, all in one room, all afternoon. One event, one afternoon, every answer.
bullets: 📍 PFEC Global Melbourne, Sydney & Adelaide offices
🎓 University representatives — ask them directly, no waiting on emails
🛂 Migration agents on site for a free migration consultation
💬 Education counsellors for real, one-on-one conversations
caption_txt.urgency: One afternoon. Every answer. Register now — link in bio.
caption_txt.contact: Come and meet Salman and the PFEC Global team at the Just Ask Expo — no appointment needed, just bring your questions.
